transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Samira Patel (Redwood SE); Diego Ramos (Redwood Product); Maya Chen (Alpine ML Eng); Rajiv Kapoor (Alpine Head of ML); Olivia Park (Alpine Infra); Tom Elliott (Alpine CTO)
Artifacts: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/optimize-quant-profiles, bench spreadsheet (will be shared)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Maya (Customer): yep, loud and clear, thanks. we got your invite, excited to see the quant stuff.
[00:07] Jordan: cool, quick intros â€” i'm Jordan, AE. Samira is our SE who owns Optimize, Diego is product. maybe a 45 minute walkthrough then Q&A.
[00:15] Samira (Redwood SE): hi all, quick agenda: why quant profiles matter, INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, demo of the Optimize console, sample benchmarks on long seqs, and next steps for a POC.
[00:24] Rajiv (Customer): sounds good. our main thing is the 2k sequence summarization workload â€” P95 latency under 900ms is ideal, we care about minimal quality regressions.
[00:34] Samira: perfect, we'll focus on that. quick note, transcription may be fuzzy on some terms â€” KV cache sometimes shows up as K-V cash in older exports.
[00:42] Diego (Product): also we'll show the auto-profile suggestion feature in Optimize â€” it suggests INT8 or FP8 based on your eval set and latency target.

[01:00] Samira: ok starting with basics â€” INT8 reduces model size aggressively, it's great for throughput and lower cost but can introduce small accuracy regressions on some heads. FP8 is newer: smaller than FP16, keeps more dynamic range, usually better quality for generation but slightly higher latency than INT8.
[01:18] Maya: is FP8 supported on Redwood Hosted or only Dedicated?
[01:22] Samira: good question â€” FP8 kernels are available on Dedicated GPUs and certain hosted instances that have the right drivers. for strict latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated so you control contention and can pin model variants.
[01:35] Olivia (Infra): if we go Dedicated, what's the network setup? we need VPC peering and KMS integration.
[01:40] Jordan: yes VPC/private deployment options exist; we also support customer-managed KMS and HSM for key control. we'll include the security playbook in the follow-up.

[02:00] Samira: demo time â€” i'm sharing the Optimize console. first panel: per-route quality vs latency curves. you can upload an eval set and run A/B across profiles.
[02:12] (screen share noise)
[02:20] Samira: here is a sample run on a 2k summary workload â€” baseline FP16 P95 = 1.1s, INT8 P95 = 650ms but with a 1.8% ROUGE drop on edge cases, FP8 P95 = 820ms with 0.5% ROUGE drop. numbers are illustrative; we'll run your exact set.
[02:45] Rajiv: ok that's helpful â€” 650ms is great, but 1.8% drop worries product. what does that look like in output?
[02:52] Samira: good point â€” let's play a couple of snippets.
[03:00] Samira: (plays example) INT8 sometimes shortens named entity spans and flips punctuation in complex sentences, FP8 generally preserves them. there's a tradeoff between throughput and fidelity.
[03:18] Maya: can Optimize do a threshold rule? like use INT8 but fallback to FP8 when confidence low?
[03:24] Diego: yes â€” Optimize can attach profile-based routing. you can set a confidence threshold or route specific prompt templates to a higher-fidelity profile. that's how many customers get cost savings while limiting regressions.

[04:00] (timestamp jump / background voice)
[04:10] Tom (CTO): one question on KV cache â€” for summarization we rely heavily on long context caching. does quantization affect KV cache correctness or size?
[04:18] Samira: quant doesn't change logical KV behavior; kernels still manage cache. FP8 may use different storage layout but the observable semantics are the same. you might see cache compression improvements with INT8 though memory layout affects eviction thresholds.
[04:35] Olivia: does batching change P95 significantly with 2k seq? we can't batch too much because of latency.
[04:42] Samira: right, continuous batching helps throughput but can hurt tail latency for single-shot API users. Optimize recommends per-route batching policies and simulates P95 for different batch sizes. for your case, small batch sizes + INT8 produced best cost/latency in our sample.

[05:20] Jordan: switching to security briefly â€” SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS are all supported. Maya: you had asked about data residency?
[05:28] Maya: yes, EU data must stay in eu-west, some customers also need retention policies.
[05:33] Jordan: we have region pinning and retention configs, and we'll share the compliance pack.

[06:00] Samira: demo â€” here's the quant profile config in the Optimize UI. you can set evaluation prompts, metric thresholds, and the rollout policy (canary percent, observed regressions threshold).
[06:18] Samira: for example, we ran a canary with INT8 at 5% traffic for 2 hours, monitor rouge/bertscore deltas and latency â€” if quality delta > 1% rollback automatically.
[06:35] Rajiv: automated rollback is nice. what metrics do you capture? raw tokens, time per token, p95/p99, and model logits?
[06:43] Samira: we capture token counts, per-token latency, p50/p95/p99, and custom eval metrics you upload. we also keep raw text diffs for failing prompts but redact PII by default.

[07:10] (more demo, screen noise)
[08:00] Maya: on the bench spreadsheet you mentioned, what fields are required?
[08:05] Samira: basic required: prompt id, reference, input length, expected target, and target metric (ROUGE/BLEU/Custom). optional: flags for hallucination, critical entity presence.
[08:18] Maya: we'll export from our internal eval harness and send the CSV.

[09:00] Jordan: quick pricing note â€” INT8 on Dedicated yields about 3-4x token cost savings vs FP16 in our experience; FP8 is usually 1.8-2.5x depending on hardware. exact numbers in the pilot pricing we'll send.
[09:18] Tom: curious if you can support mixed precision in the same endpoint â€” some routes INT8, others FP8?
[09:23] Diego: yes, routes can map to profiles. a single API layer can route to profile variants; the runtime handles model variant selection and KV cache compatibility where possible.

[10:00] (timestamp)
[10:12] Rajiv: any known regressions with hallucination increase for INT8?
[10:18] Samira: occasionally INT8 can increase hallucination in low-context edge cases. that's why we recommend targeted eval sets covering hallucination-sensitive prompts. Optimize flags prompts with >X delta for review.
[10:32] Maya: what's the turnaround to spin up a Dedicated environment for a pilot?
[10:36] Jordan: typically 2-3 weeks for reserved pool provisioning and VPC setup, shorter if you accept hosted sandbox options.

[11:00] (mid-call recap)
[11:05] Jordan: recap â€” customer will share 2k test set, Redwood will run INT8/FP8 bench on Dedicated sample hardware, Samira will share the spreadsheet and suggested profile. we'll follow up with pricing and security docs.
[11:15] Samira: i'll also include a sample canary policy and notes about rolling back on quality deltas.

[11:40] Maya: detail â€” for our evaluation, please include P95 and P99, ROUGE-L and a custom entity-presence metric.
[11:46] Samira: noted. any hard blockers for you folks?
[11:50] Olivia: KMS integration is mandatory, and we need SAML for SSO.
[11:55] Jordan: we'll include integration steps; we support customer-managed KMS and SAML.

[12:10] Rajiv: last technical Q â€” will quantization affect latency variability across tokens? we see spikes near long prompts.
[12:16] Samira: we see more variability with larger batch sizes and long KV cache hits. INT8 can reduce mean latency but sometimes increases variance if kernel fallback happens; Optimize simulates this and flags problematic prompt patterns.

[13:00] (closing)
[13:05] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-ups â€” Samira bench, Jordan pricing & security, and we'll set up the POC scoping for Aug 12.
[13:15] Tom: thanks, appreciate the depth.
[13:18] Maya: thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: a few technical terms transcribed oddly (FP8 sometimes as F P eight, KV cache as K V cash), small filler words and overlapping talk.

End of transcript.
